transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-03
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 53 minutes
Attendees: Maya T. (Redwood AE), Carlos R. (Redwood SE), Janel P. (CSM), Oliver G., Meera S., Evan L., Tanya B., Samir D.

Summary:
Short intake to walk Whitestone through Redwood's answers for the customer's vendor assurance form, focus on data residency options, KMS/HSM integration, audit logs retention, and the SIG/CAIQ evidence plan. Agreed to follow up with an evidence mapping spreadsheet and SOC 2 artifacts.

Topics:
- SIG v2 walkthrough and which questions need attestations vs evidence
- SOC 2 Type II artifacts and pen test cadence
- KMS integration options: customer-managed keys (BYOK) vs Redwood-managed KMS; HSM options for Private deployments
- Data residency/residency controls (EU vs US, region pinning, subnet controls)
- Audit logs, retention windows, SIEM integration, and role-level access (RBAC/SSO)
- Next steps and evidence delivery plan

Action Items (quick):
- Carlos to build the evidence mapping per SIG section
- Maya to share SOC 2 summary and pen test note
- Oliver to confirm residency constraints and internal approvers

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Thompson: Hey everyone, thanks for making time. we, uh, we wanted to make this pretty focused — walkthrough your vendor assurance form and highlight the bits that typically make teams pause, right? residency and KMS mostly.

[00:18] Oliver Grant: yeah thanks Maya. we got a pile of questions from procurement and compliance. primary ask, just to be super clear, is we need EU-only residency for PII in the pilot, at least for the first 12 months. Any hybrid options?

[00:32] Maya Thompson: absolutely, short answer yes. Redwood supports region pinning for hosted, and for Dedicated and Private you can choose a VPC-only deployment in eu-west-1 or eu-central-1. note though, we do sometimes refer to "Redwood Priv" internally for private deploys, sorry that is shorthand.

[00:47] Evan Luo: quick Q — if we do hosted but pin to EU, does any metadata or logs still touch US control plane? there was mention of a control plane service.

[00:57] Carlos Ruiz: good call out. currently the control plane touches a narrow set of metadata (billing, account config). we have an option for a private control plane for Enterprise or Private deployments which keeps metadata in your VPC. for hosted EU-pin we do retain minimal operational telemetry in the control plane in the region — but we can show the dataflow.

[01:14] Meera Shah: and is that covered under SOC2? procurement is asking how we can demonstrate that separation.

[01:21] Maya Thompson: SOC 2 Type II covers a lot of the controls; we'll send the SOC 2 summary. note that SOC 2 attests to operational controls and we also provide a CAIQ-style mapping for cloud controls that you can attach to the SIG answers.

[01:35] Tanya Bhat: on the CAIQ vs SIG point, which do you prefer submitting? our vendor team usually wants SIG but the security folks asked for CAIQ too sometimes.

[01:44] Carlos Ruiz: we can provide both. SIG is the supplier questionnaire; CAIQ/Consensus is more cloud provider-style. for Redwood we typically map our controls into the SIG and produce a CAIQ export for cloud-focused sections — quick wins are tokenization, network segmentation, and KMS sections.

[01:59] Oliver Grant: KMS, yes — that's where procurement got nervous. We need BYOK with key ownership and key rotation logs. how do you integrate with our KMS?

[02:09] Carlos Ruiz: multiple paths. for Private/Dedicated we support direct HSM-backed BYOK via customer-rotated keys with KMS wrapping. for hosted, we offer a customer-managed key option through our cloud KMS integration — redwood-keystore will reference your key. caveat: hosted BYOK maps to our tokenization flow and we rotate envelopes on our side, but the master key never leaves your KMS.

[02:32] Samir Das: sorry, can you say HSM again — is that H-S-M? our legal wrote HSMs as H-S-M, wonder if that's the same.

[02:37] Maya Thompson: yes, HSM — hardware security module. we can provide evidence of HSM usage for Private deployments where you bring your HSM or we integrate with cloud HSMs like AWS CloudHSM or Azure Dedicated HSM.

[02:47] Evan Luo: what's the audit trail look like for key usage — we need logs that show which key ID was used per request and timestamps for rotation events.

[02:56] Carlos Ruiz: we emit KMS access events to the audit log; for Private deployments you can route logs to your SIEM via syslog/S3 export. for hosted, we provide an audit-export with key usage events, and we can include KMS key ID, operation (encrypt/decrypt), and timestamp. retention is configurable up to 7 years for Enterprise customers, default is 90 days.

[03:16] Meera Shah: retention up to 7 years is good. procurement will want to see that in writing.

[03:22] Maya Thompson: we'll put that in the evidence pack. also note that if you require EU-only storage for logs, we can configure the log export to land in an EU bucket under your account for Private/Dedicated.

[03:38] Oliver Grant: can we talk RBAC and SSO — our auditors want to know how granular roles are and whether SAML can map to groups.

[03:48] Carlos Ruiz: we support SSO SAML 2.0 and SCIM provisioning for groups. RBAC maps to roles at the org, team, and token level. e.g., you can create a role that only allows model inference but not model upload or rollout. we also have token-scoped permissions for service-to-service integrations.

[04:05] Tanya Bhat: is there a separation between admin accounts and service accounts in the audit logs? auditors ask to see that distinction.

[04:11] Carlos Ruiz: yes, audit events include actor type: user vs service. Events also record the actor identity, the action, resource, and originating IP. we can export a sample audit log file for you to review — that tends to reassure auditors.

[04:27] Meera Shah: sample audit log would be great. also, do you do MFA enforced for admin roles?

[04:32] Maya Thompson: yes, MFA is enforced for all org admins and we recommend it for service account principals where interactive logins occur. we can provide our SSO/SAML config doc and screenshots.

[04:44] Oliver Grant: about the SIG — a lot of the questions want an evidence item rather than just a yes. can you give examples of evidence we can attach?

[04:51] Carlos Ruiz: sure — typical items: SOC 2 report (redacted), pen test summary, role-based access matrix, SSO metadata and SCIM provisioning logs, KMS key rotation policy doc, HSM attestation or cloud HSM config, network segmentation diagrams, sample audit logs, SIEM integration playbook, and product architecture diagram with data flows. we'll list which are attestation vs raw evidence.

[05:18] Samir Das: about the pen tests — how often, and can you share the most recent scope?

[05:24] Maya Thompson: we run annual third-party pen tests and quarterly internal scans. we'll share the most recent executive summary and the scope; full reports are under NDA typically, but we can provide a redacted copy.

[05:36] Evan Luo: another technical question — KV cache and prefixes, does that store any customer data in a shared cache? our compliance team is worried about cross-tenant leakage.

[05:46] Carlos Ruiz: good catch. the runtime uses memory-isolated KV caches per model instance and per-tenant namespaces. we also encrypt caches at rest in Private and Dedicated. for hosted, we use multi-tenant caches but segmented and encrypted; we can run a dedicated cache pool for higher isolation if requested.

[06:04] Oliver Grant: dedicated pools — would that affect latency? our latency SLO is 200ms median for the pilot.

[06:12] Carlos Ruiz: dedicated pools reduce noisy neighbor risk and give more predictable latency; we can meet 200ms median for the pilot with Dedicated capacity. we'll model throughput and estimate GPU footprint in the follow-up.

[06:25] Meera Shah: any mentions of model weights storage — are model artifacts considered customer data when we fine-tune?

[06:32] Maya Thompson: if you fine-tune within a Private deployment on your infra, weights live in your storage. for hosted we treat customer fine-tunes as customer-specific artifacts; access controls enforce that only your org tokens can access those model versions. we can include the retention policy for training artifacts.

[06:50] Tanya Bhat: data residency with backups — do backups ever cross region for disaster recovery, and how is that controlled?

[06:58] Carlos Ruiz: backups are region-local by default. cross-region replication is an opt-in DR feature and requires explicit config; for EU-only constraint we would disable cross-region replication. we'll capture that in the evidence notes.

[07:14] Oliver Grant: about encryption in transit and at rest — is that TLS 1.3 and AES-256? procurement asked for cipher suites and FIPS compatibility.

[07:24] Carlos Ruiz: yes TLS 1.3 by default; AES-256-GCM for at-rest encryption. FIPS mode is available for Private deployments — it depends on the underlying OS/kernel and HSM configuration. we can include a cipher suite list and FIPS statement.

[07:39] Meera Shah: for SIG question 4.3 about incident response — auditors want to see mean time to detect/contain. can you provide those metrics?

[07:47] Maya Thompson: we can provide SOC metrics at a high level — MTTR for incidents is tracked, and we have playbooks. exact numbers can be provided in the SOC summary and incident response section; we can also map the SIG question to the relevant section.

[07:59] Evan Luo: do you have a defined breach notification timeline? our contracts require 72 hours for material incidents.

[08:05] Maya Thompson: yes, 72-hour notification for qualified incidents; we also have an escalation path and we can include point-of-contact templates.

[08:14] Oliver Grant: on the technical evidence, is there any sample of the SIEM integration? we use Splunk; they want to see a sample ingestion template.

[08:24] Carlos Ruiz: we have a Splunk ingestion playbook and a sample query set for common audit events. I'll attach that to the evidence pack.

[08:33] Meera Shah: procurement also asked about subprocessor lists — do you list cloud infra providers and any analytics vendors?

[08:41] Maya Thompson: yes, we maintain a subprocessor list and a data processing addendum. common subprocessors include cloud providers (we'll name them per region) and a monitoring vendor for runtime telemetry. we can give the DPA and the full subprocessor list.

[08:58] Samir Das: for legal, is there a model of indemnification or liability caps tied to data residency breaches?

[09:05] Maya Thompson: those are negotiable on enterprise contracts; we'll include standard liability language and can flag points to legal for negotiation.

[09:17] Evan Luo: micro question on tokenization and embeddings — if we generate embeddings for search, are those stored with PII stripped?

[09:25] Carlos Ruiz: embeddings are stored with metadata; we recommend pseudonymization before embedding if you have PII constraints. we can also opt to not persist embeddings and use ephemeral pipelines. we'll document options.

[09:35] Oliver Grant: okay, so next from our side is we need a mapping that shows which SIG question gets which artifact. can you prioritize the SIG questions that typically block procurement?

[09:44] Maya Thompson: yes — typically blocking SIG items are key management (BYOK + HSM), data residency and backups, incident response and notification, subprocessor transparency, and access controls (RBAC/SSO). we'll mark those in the mapping.

[10:00] Meera Shah: timeline — procurement wants evidence in two weeks to hit the December procurement window. is that realistic?

[10:07] Maya Thompson: yes, two weeks is doable for the evidence pack (SOC summary, pen test exec summary, sample audit logs, SSO metadata, KMS policy, and the SIG-to-evidence mapping). anything requiring legal review might take longer.

[10:20] Carlos Ruiz: I'll flag any items that need redaction or NDA before we send full reports.

[10:28] Oliver Grant: quick on the SLA — can you include availability SLO and runbook excerpt?

[10:34] Maya Thompson: absolutely, we'll include the SLA excerpt and the runbook summary for failover and fallbacks.

[10:41] Meera Shah: one more technical: how do you handle model drift monitoring and quality regressions? procurement asked since they intend to rely on outputs.

[10:49] Carlos Ruiz: Redwood Optimize includes quality monitoring; we can tie results back to specific prompt sets and alert on regression. we can provide an eval report sample and configured alert thresholds.

[11:00] Tanya Bhat: back to SSO — can you do multiple SAML IdPs for different org units?

[11:06] Carlos Ruiz: yes, multiple IdPs are supported with mapping rules. we can show a config example.

[11:14] Oliver Grant: Customer's compliance likes to see separation of duties. can you provide a role matrix sample?

[11:20] Maya Thompson: yes, we'll include a role matrix showing admin, auditor, devops, and service roles and examples of allowed actions.

[11:29] Evan Luo: is there any ongoing telemetry that Redwood collects that might include API call payload metadata?

[11:37] Carlos Ruiz: operational telemetry includes request size and timing metadata but not full user payloads unless opted in for debugging. we can provide a telemetry data dictionary.

[11:50] Meera Shah: can you confirm retention of logs for the pilot — default 90 days, but need 2 years for certain logs would that be extra cost?

[11:58] Maya Thompson: extended retention is an enterprise add-on. we'll include cost guidance in the follow-up.

[12:08] Oliver Grant: any special compliance for healthcare data or PCI? we might have downstream customers in healthcare.

[12:16] Carlos Ruiz: Redwood has a HIPAA-compliant posture for Private deployments and BAA options; PCI controls depend on the integration surface but we can map relevant PCI controls. we'll surface the compliance matrix.

[12:30] Tanya Bhat: question about environment separation — dev vs prod — what guarantees are there that test data won't bleed into prod?

[12:38] Carlos Ruiz: environments are logically separated, with separate deployments and storage. for hosted we provide separate orgs and tokens; for Dedicated/Private you get separate clusters and storage. we'll include architecture diagrams.

[12:52] Oliver Grant: ok, about evidence delivery format — our intake system prefers attachments with short descriptions rather than links. can you provide a ZIP with filenames that match SIG sections?

[13:01] Maya Thompson: yes we can. we'll structure the zip with a README that maps files to SIG question numbers. Carlos will own the mapping.

[13:10] Meera Shah: procurement asked if you have any SLA credits or remedies language already drafted.

[13:17] Maya Thompson: yes, standard SLO credit table is in the contract playbook. I'll attach the excerpt.

[13:24] Oliver Grant: any blockers on privacy impact assessments?

[13:30] Carlos Ruiz: we can provide a privacy impact statement for the intended use case. sometimes that's produced on a per-customer basis but we have a template we can adapt.

[13:38] Samir Das: legal follow-up — will you accept a redline on the DPA?

[13:44] Maya Thompson: yes, we'll accept and review redlines. major changes may require legal review turnaround.

[13:52] Meera Shah: if we need a demo of the SSO/admin console for auditors, can we get a short session?

[13:58] Janel Park: absolutely, we can schedule a 30-min admin console demo and show the audit log export process.

[14:06] Oliver Grant: okay good. any final thoughts from the Redwood team?

[14:11] Carlos Ruiz: I'll start the evidence spreadsheet and mark priority SIG questions. I also want to call out a minor transcribing note: in our product there's a "KV cache" that is often called "key value cache" but it's not KMS. so we'll make sure the mapping is clear.

[14:26] Maya Thompson: great. to recap — Redwood will share SOC 2 summary, pen test exec summary (redacted), SIEM ingestion playbook, SSO/SCIM config, KMS key rotation policy and sample audit logs, and the SIG-to-evidence worksheet. we'll follow up with dates for the KMS deep-dive and admin demo.

[14:45] Oliver Grant: perfect. we'll aim to reconvene after reviewing evidence. thanks everyone.

[14:50] Meera Shah: thanks all.

[15:00] End of recording

Notes on transcription: occasional mislabels and filler present; some technical terms shortened (Priv, KV cache). timestamps are approximate, and longer sections were summarized for clarity in the header.
